subject: Audit logs archival strategy and on-demand provisioning for BlueHarbor Health
messages:
From: Laura Jensen <laura.jensen@thirdparty-audits.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: BlueHarbor Security Team <compliance@blueharborhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: audit log export scope and retention policy for upcoming SOC2 re-audit

Rishi —

Thanks for taking this on. BlueHarbor's SOC2 re-audit is scheduled for the week of May 9. We need the following to be confirmed and, if possible, an initial sample export to validate format and checksums: 

- What event categories are retained in your admin/audit logging pipeline (who, what, when, where) — specifically: user sign-ins, admin role changes, API key creations, model deployments, operator console actions, and streaming session traces.
- Canonical retention windows per category (and whether they are TTL-based or archival with immutability).
- Export delivery options and expected SLA for an on-demand forensic snapshot covering 2026-11-01 through 2027-03-31. Preferred formats: newline-delimited JSON (jsonl) or Parquet.
- Evidence integrity: manifest format, hashing algorithm, signed manifest options.
- For legal holds / litigation preservation, does Redwood pause TTLs or create a separate immutable archive? If separate, how long can it be retained?

Please include any redaction options we should be aware of (PII minimization), and whether exports can be encrypted with BlueHarbor-managed KMS keys (customer-provided).

If you can get a 24–48 hour sample extract for the date range above (small slice, e.g., 2027-03-25 to 2027-03-28) that demonstrates the manifest + checksum workflow, that would be ideal. Attach a sample manifest stub if available.

Laura Jensen
Senior Auditor, Trident Compliance
laura.jensen@thirdparty-audits.com

Attachment: request_checklist.pdf (referenced, not included)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Laura Jensen <laura.jensen@thirdparty-audits.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, BlueHarbor Security Team <compliance@blueharborhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: audit log export scope and retention policy for upcoming SOC2 re-audit

Laura / BlueHarbor —

Appreciate the clear checklist. Below is a high-level summary of how we record and make admin/audit activity available. I’ll follow up with an export run plan and a sample manifest by EOD.

What we log (canonical categories):
- Authentication events (login successes/failures, MFA events) — retained 13 months by default (TTL-based primary store).
- Identity & access changes (role grants, deprovisioning, API key lifecycle) — retained 13 months; privileged-change events are replicated to long-term storage on request.
- Admin console actions (model deploys, rollout changes, canary toggles, route config) — retained 13 months; operator-level detailed traces (stacked operator commands, console logs) retained 90 days unless an enterprise retention add-on is purchased.
- System telemetry about streaming sessions / KV cache misses — kept 90 days; aggregated tokens/latency metrics kept longer in metrics telemetry but are not part of the admin event feed.
- Forensic operator trails (superuser sessions / direct GPU job control) — by default 36 months for enterprise customers when enabled; otherwise 13 months.

Retention model and legal hold behavior:
- Default store is TTL-based S3 buckets with lifecycle rules (immutable object option not applied by default).
- For legal holds or litigation preservation we create an attested archive snapshot (immutable, HMAC + KMS-wrapped) that suspends TTL deletion for the snapshot's objects. That snapshot can be retained for a negotiated window (typical enterprise carveout: up to 7 years).

Export options and delivery SLA:
- Export formats: jsonl (newline-delimited JSON), Parquet (partitioned by date && event_type), and compressed archives (gz).
- Delivery methods: encrypted SFTP push, pre-signed HTTPS URL (time-limited), or direct transfer to a customer-owned S3/GCS bucket using STS temporary creds.
- Integrity & signing: we produce a manifest.csv/jsonl listing files, record counts, start/end timestamps, and SHA-256 checksums for each file. We can also sign the manifest with Redwood's export signing key (optional: provide an external key for encryption).
- SLA: standard on-demand snapshot turnaround is 72 hours. For SOC2 audit-critical requests we offer a prioritized 24-hour SLA with approval from Compliance & Ops (expedited process available).

Redaction & PII handling:
- Exports can be filtered by event type and redact / pseudonymize fields at export time (email hashing, user-id pseudonymization). The export runbook documents exact field-level options.

Next steps (action items):
1) I’ll produce a small sample extract for 2027-03-25 -> 2027-03-28 in jsonl format with an unsigned manifest attached for validation. Target: within 48 hours.
2) Kimberly, can you confirm infra capacity and whether we need a privileged-run window for the requested full-range export (2026-11-01 -> 2027-03-31)?
3) Neha, I’ll need QA sign-off on redaction options for BlueHarbor before we export anything with PII removed.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security & Privacy Operations
Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Attachment: sample_manifest.jsonl (placeholder — will send actual sample)

Cc: BlueHarbor Security Team <compliance@blueharborhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: audit log export scope and retention policy for upcoming SOC2 re-audit

Rishi / Neha —

Confirmed. Infra can run the sample extraction and a scoped full-range run, but we need to coordinate a low-impact maintenance window for the full export (high IO). Proposed timeline below: 

- Sample extract (2027-03-25 -> 2027-03-28): start within 24 hours, delivery via pre-signed URL, compressed jsonl, signed manifest attached.
- Full-range snapshot (2026-11-01 -> 2027-03-31): schedule for 2027-04-10 06:00 UTC; estimated prep + run = 4–6 hours. Delivery via BlueHarbor-owned S3 endpoint using STS temporary creds (preferred for large transfers).

Operational notes: 
- We will produce both a raw event set and a redacted version if requested. Redaction is applied as a post-export transform step (so raw remains immutable in the snapshot).
- Checksums: SHA-256 per-file + signed manifest; optional HMAC attestation if BlueHarbor requires a shared secret handshake.
- Chain-of-custody: we will produce an export manifest with exporter ID, run timestamp, operator run log, and the artifact HMAC. That will be included as a top-level signed file (signed_manifest-20270409.sig).

I’ve attached our internal runbook stub and will open HS-7219 with the export request details. Rishi — please confirm you want the prioritized 24-hour SLA for the full snapshot or the default 72-hour window.

Kimberly Park
Director, Infrastructure Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: export_runbook.md

Laura / BlueHarbor —

Quick update & confirmation:

- Sample extract has been generated for 2027-03-25 -> 2027-03-28 and is available at the secure drive link (see related_links). File: blueharbor_sample_20270325-28.jsonl.gz. Manifest and unsigned checksum file included.
- Full snapshot scheduled: 2027-04-10 06:00 UTC -> estimated completion 12:00 UTC. We will use BlueHarbor-owned S3 with STS temporary credentials for transfer. If BlueHarbor instead prefers SFTP push, let us know and we will switch the delivery method.
- We can apply a legal-hold snapshot once the transfer completes. This will create an immutable archive that suspends lifecycle deletion for the snapshot object set. Proposed retention window for the hold: 7 years (can be shortened/lengthened by contract amendment).
- SLA: BlueHarbor has requested audit-priority handling — we have approved the 24-hour prioritized workflow for the full snapshot. 

Attached: signed_manifest-20270409.sig (signed top-level manifest), sample_manifest.jsonl, and internal export_runbook.md.

Action items for BlueHarbor:
1) Confirm delivery endpoint preference (S3 bucket vs SFTP).
2) Confirm whether you want the redacted export in addition to raw. If redaction requested, provide the exact pseudonymization rules you prefer (email hashing vs full redaction).
3) If you require KMS-wrapped objects under your key, we need the KMS ARN and cross-account grant details by 2027-04-09 20:00 UTC.

Thanks — we’ll standby for your confirmation and will proceed with the scheduled run.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security & Privacy Operations
Redwood Inference
